title: FA/61/2022 of GEETA Vs MITHLESH SAHU ALIAS RAJKUMAR

JUDGMENT: ( p er Hon 'b le Ju st ice Mr . Rak esh Th ap liy al)

The respondent-husband is present in the Court
today.
2) The appellant-wife has com e up in appeal
against the judgm ent and decree dated 17.02.2020,
passed by Judge, Fam ily Court, Haldwani, District Nainital,

2024:UHC:6219-DB
in Civil Case No. 170 OF 2013, titled as 'Mithlesh Sahu @
Rajkum ar Vs Sm t. Geeta', filed under Section 13(i) of the
Hindu Marriage Act, whereby the divorce petition filed by
the respondent-husband has been allowed, and a decree
of divorce was granted in favour of the respondent.
3) The m arriage between the parties was
solem nized on 30.06.2010. The parties are living
separately since 2013. There is no issue from this
m arriage.
4) Keeping in view the above fact, reference can
now be m ade to a recent Suprem e Court judgm ent in the
case of Rak esh Ram an Vs Kav it a, 2 0 2 3 SCC On Lin e SC
4 9 7 , decided on 26.04.2023. I n that case the m arriage
was solem nized on 16.04.1994, and there was no child
from this m arriage, and the parties m erely stayed
together for four years, and by the tim e the m atter went
to the Suprem e Court the m arriage had been 25 years
old. There was no child from the wedlock. The Suprem e
Court held that the m atrim onial bond had com pletely
broken and was beyond repair, and the fact that it was
long separation and absence of cohabitation and the
com plete breakdown of all m eaningful bonds has to be
read as cruelty under Section 13(1)(ia) of the 1955 Act.
 2

2024:UHC:6219-DB
Since the dissolution of m arriage would affect only the two
parties, and there was no child out of the wedlock, the
Suprem e Court allowed the appeal of the husband, and
held that the m arriage stood dissolved. Keeping in view
the incom e of the appellant, perm anent alim ony of rupees
30 lakhs was awarded to the wife.
5) I n the case in hand, there is no child born out of
the m arriage between the parties, which took place on
30.06.2010, and as on today in the year 2024, alm ost 14
years have gone by. I t is a dead m arriage, and in the
Suprem e Court judgm ent referred hereinabove, constantly
it has been held that in such circum stances where the
m arriage between the parties is only in nam e, and the
sam e has been wrecked beyond the hope of salvage, it
would be in public interest to declare such a m arriage as
defunct. The long period of continuous separation has
resulted in the m atrim onial bond wrecked beyond repair.
The m arriage has becom e a fiction. I t is only supported
by a legal tie.
6) Counsel for the respondent states that there is
irretrievable breakdown of m arriage between the parties,
and there is no chance of resum ption of m atrim onial ties
between them . This Court also tried to resolve the
 3

2024:UHC:6219-DB
dispute between the parties, and had sent both the parties
for m ediation. The Mediator has filed his report dated
05.07.2024, stating therein that 'm ediation proceedings
are closes, as unsuccessful'.
7) At this stage, counsel for the respondent-husband states that the respondent is ready to pay an
am ount of Rs.1,50,000/ - (rupees one lakh fifty thousand
only) towards perm anent alim ony to the appellant-wife.
8) Keeping in view the above statem ent, as also
the fact that the respondent-husband is a daily wager, it
will be in the interest of justice to dispose of this appeal
by directing the respondent-husband to pay an am ount of
Rs.1,50,000/ - towards perm anent alim ony to the
appellant-wife. Said am ount will be paid to the appellant-wife within fifteen days from today. Counsel for the
respondent will inform this Court regarding the paym ent
so m ade within the tim e stipulated.
9) With the direction as above, the First Appeal
stands disposed. The decree of divorce granted in favour
of the respondent-husband will attain finality now.
However, it is m ade clear, that the appellant-wife will

10) Pending application(s) if any, also stands
disposed of.
